$comment: What the public PRs did, in plain words. Facts and numbers are taken from the PR descriptions (public, GitHub). Each card links its PRs.

cards.title: Rules that actually reach the agent
cards.problem: Always-on MCP server instructions had grown to ~2,199 tokens; the client truncated them past ~1,000, so rules silently dropped, and nothing forced the agent to load the right guide.
cards.built: A thin router: hard invariants on top plus a names-only routing table, and guidance forced through channels the client always delivers — tool descriptions and tool results.
cards.result: Instructions 2,199 → 506 tokens (−77%); dashboard and metric rules now reach the agent when it touches those tools.

cards.title: Agents configure the platform — only valid configs get saved
cards.problem: Agent-generated configuration could pass validation, save and still break at runtime: a mobile metric that shows no value, a widget title rendered as a raw localization key.
cards.built: Deterministic validation in the MCP layer before save: a typed contract for business-rule static filters, checks that refuse metrics the mobile runtime cannot execute, and a gate for titles bound to unresolvable keys — each with a diagnostic that names the missing path.
cards.result: These failures are now rejected when the agent authors the config, not discovered later by users.

cards.title: One feature, three repositories: code, guidance, decision
cards.problem: Apps created by agents landed in a section only system administrators can see — the placement question was never asked.
cards.built: Split by responsibility: new MCP commands and contracts in clio, a guidance article and routing edits in clio-knowledge, and in the app-development toolkit navigation placement and audience became a required discovery question.
cards.result: The decision is made during discovery, before anything is created, and each repo can be reviewed on its own.
